## Intended use

Drafting, review and approval of regulatory content, including the governed transitions that make a draft an approved record.

Surfaces in scope: `document-authoring`, `authoring-engine`, `template-library`, `review`, `regulatory-workspace`

**Reading the impact column.** `direct` means the software itself affects the
integrity, authenticity or content of a regulated record, or decides who may act
on one. `indirect` means it supports that work without producing the record.
The distinction sets the assurance effort: a direct-impact requirement cannot be
discharged by inspection, and the gate refuses a registry that tries.

## Requirement detail

### URS-AUTHORING-01 — The system shall accept requests to the authoring store only from a caller presenting a verified access-class bearer token whose organization membership is re-checked live, and shall derive the acting identity, roles and tenant solely from that token, discarding any caller-supplied x-roles, x-user-email or x-tenant-id header before any handler runs.

**Intended use.** A regulatory author, reviewer or approver signs in and every act they perform on a CTD/eCTD document is attributed to them and confined to their organization; attribution on the resulting record is what a Part 11 inspection traces back to a person.

**If it fails.** A client that asserts its own roles, email or tenant in HTTP headers edits, approves or exports another organization's governed document, and the audit trail names whoever the request claimed to be. A regulator would then believe a named individual authored or approved content they never touched.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-AUTHORING-02 — The system shall decide every edit, comment, review, approve and manage-permissions MUTATION request against the document's own permission grants (OWNER, AUTHOR, REVIEWER, APPROVER, VIEWER) plus a platform-admin allowlist, refusing an unknown object with 404, an immutable document with 409 and an unauthorized principal with 403, and shall record every grant and revoke as an audit row whose write outcome is reported to the caller; read requests (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) are scoped by tenant only and are not decided against the object's grants.

**Intended use.** A document owner controls who may draft, review or approve a specific regulatory document; the record of who held which authority, and when, is the evidence that an approval was applied by someone entitled to apply it.

**If it fails.** A VIEWER or an unrelated organization member edits or approves a governed document because the decision was made on a global role rather than on the object's grants, or a permission change is lost silently so the authority history cannot be reconstructed.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-AUTHORING-03 — The system shall record every change to authored section content as an append-only revision carrying the content SHA-256, the previous chain hash, the author, the write path that produced it and the citation set in force — written inside the content transaction on the interactive save, revert and template-apply paths, and written after the content has already committed on the AI-draft-accept path (where a failure is logged and tolerated) and on section create — shall refuse UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the revision table at the database engine, and shall expose a verification endpoint that recomputes every hash and reports the exact revision at which the chain breaks.

**Intended use.** A reviewer or inspector opens a section's history to establish what the text said at each point, who wrote it and that no revision has been altered or removed since — the 21 CFR 11.10(e) audit trail for the document's content.

**If it fails.** A revision is edited or deleted in place, or a new revision is written unchained, and the history still reads as complete. An inspector would believe the displayed history is the whole record of how the filed text came to say what it says.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-AUTHORING-04 — The system shall refuse every mutation of section content on a document whose status is FROZEN or APPROVED or whose lock timestamp is set, applying one canonical guard — read on the connection pool immediately before the write, not inside the write's transaction — to the interactive save, revert and AI-draft-accept paths via a single prefix middleware, and an equivalent inline parent-status check to section create, and shall refuse the write when the document's status or the section's parent cannot be read.

**Intended use.** Once a document is sealed under a content hash or covered by an approval signature, its content is part of the signed record; an author must be told to create a new version rather than being allowed to change sealed text.

**If it fails.** Text is typed into and saved onto a document the toolbar shows as Frozen, so the freeze snapshot's content hash and any signature applied over it certify content that has since changed — the seal becomes a claim the system cannot support.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-AUTHORING-05 — The system shall apply an electronic signature to a document only when the signer is the token-verified principal, holds an organization role on the signing-authority allowlist (checked before the credential so the endpoint cannot act as a PIN oracle), supplies a reason and a meaning drawn from the closed signature-meaning vocabulary, and passes bcrypt PIN re-authentication; and shall persist the signature, its content hash, the frozen snapshot it covers, the workflow-step advance and the hash-chained audit row in one transaction that rolls back entirely on any failure.

**Intended use.** An approver signs off a regulatory document; the stored signature is the 21 CFR 11.50/11.70 manifestation that binds a named, authorized person and a stated meaning to a specific immutable version of that record.

**If it fails.** An authenticated member without signing authority applies an APPROVER signature, or a signature is stored while the workflow step or the audit row it depends on was never written, leaving a signed record with no traceable approval act or a meaning outside the governed vocabulary.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-AUTHORING-06 — The system shall refuse with 409 any export of an authoring document that is not sealed (status FROZEN or APPROVED, or an explicit lock timestamp), shall attribute the export to the token-verified principal with no request-body fallback, and shall record a hash of the delivered artifact bytes on the export-history row.

**Intended use.** An exported DOCX/PDF leaves the platform as a filing artifact carrying the 11.50 signature manifest; only a sealed record has an immutable snapshot and certified signatures behind it to justify that presentation.

**If it fails.** A DRAFT or IN_REVIEW document exports byte-for-byte like an approved one with reviewer signatures appended, so unapproved, still-editable content circulates as a certified record, attributed to whoever the request body named.

### URS-AUTHORING-08 — The system shall record author, source and machine provenance spans for every authored-content write inside the same transaction as the content, shall roll the content write back when the recorded spans do not cover the saved text, and shall attribute machine-generated clauses to the machine author — as accepted-by-actor where a human accepted them and as unasserted machine draft where none did — rather than to the human actor.

**Intended use.** Every sentence of a regulatory document must trace to where it came from — a cited source, the named human author, or a model draft a human accepted — which is what a reviewer relies on when asked to stand behind a claim in a filing.

**If it fails.** Text generated by a model is persisted attributed to the human whose session saved it, or content commits while its provenance write fails, so a filing contains claims whose origin the organization cannot reconstruct or, worse, attributes to a person who never asserted them.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-AUTHORING-09 — The system shall refuse with 409 a section save that supplies an expected-last-modified timestamp which does not match the stored row, changing nothing and returning the current timestamp; the check is opt-in, so a save that supplies no parseable timestamp still replaces the section's content unconditionally.

**Intended use.** Two people commonly work the same CTD section during a review round; a writer must be told their basis moved and be able to reload rather than discover later that a colleague's paragraphs are gone.

**If it fails.** The later save overwrites the whole section, the overwrite enters the hash-chained revision ledger as an ordinary authored revision, and nothing downstream shows that a collision occurred — the chain verifies and the content is wrong.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-AUTHORING-10 — The system shall the Document Authoring surface shall render a failed read as a failure to read and never as an absence of data, showing distinct states for loading, failed and genuinely empty on the document list, the section list, the revision history, the comment thread, the sources rail and the audit rail, and shall state on a failed audit-trail read that no conclusion about governed acts can be drawn.

**Intended use.** A reviewer opens the audit rail or the revision history of a governed document to confirm what was done to it; the screen must never let a service outage read as evidence that nothing happened.

**If it fails.** The audit rail shows 'No audit events yet' and the history rail shows 'No prior revisions' because the GET returned 500, and a reviewer or inspector concludes that no governed acts or revisions exist for a record whose Part 11 trail was in fact written correctly and merely unreadable.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-AUTHORING-12 — The system shall the Document Authoring surface shall obtain a stated reason for change from the author before the first save of an editing session on a section and send it with each governed save, and shall never substitute a default or generated reason for an author's own content edit; the one save the author does not perform — applying a comment anchor — carries a fixed system reason naming that mechanism instead.

**Intended use.** 21 CFR 11.10(d)/(e) asks why a governed record changed; the reason captured here is what the document's version ledger and audit trail record alongside the content hash before and after.

**If it fails.** Saves reach the governed store with no reason, so the audit trail records only that a change happened and not why, or the client invents a reason and the record attributes a justification to an author who never gave one.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-AUTHORING-90 — The system shall return a visitor with no session from the Authoring surface `review` to sign-in, and shall render that surface only once a session is established.

**Intended use.** A regulatory user reaches Authoring through an authenticated session. The record this surface exposes is a regulated one, so an unauthenticated visitor must be returned to sign-in rather than shown any part of it.

**If it fails.** The surface renders for a visitor with no session, exposing a regulated record to an unidentified person and breaking the attribution every audit entry depends on.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high
